svg.title: A credible interval and a confidence interval on one axis
svg.desc: The Beta(28, 16) posterior for the germination rate with its central 95 percent credible interval shaded, and below it the classical 95 percent confidence interval for the same forty seeds, with what each interval claims written underneath.
svg.text: Forty seeds, twenty-six germinated: two intervals, two claims
0.4907 to 0.7702. Given this model and the Beta(2, 2) prior, there is a 0.95 posterior
probability that pi lies in THIS interval. The marker is the posterior mean 0.6364.
0.5022 to 0.7978. The recipe that built it covers the true pi in 95 percent of repeated
Both statements are correct. Only the first is a probability about this particular interval; the second
is a property of the procedure.
The credible interval sits a little lower and is a little narrower, because the Beta(2, 2) prior pulls gently toward one half.
